name: Talitha
overview: Talitha was a young female child, specifically twelve years old, known as the daughter of a synagogue official who was healed by Jesus. Her story is primarily noted for the miraculous healing she experienced, as recorded in Mark 5. She is not associated with any particular tribe or surname in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Talitha' means 'little girl' and is presented as a title rather than a given name. This designation highlights her youth and innocence at the time of her healing, as noted in Mark 5:41.
familyAndRelationships: Talitha is explicitly identified as the daughter of Jairus, a synagogue official, according to Mark 5:23. Scripture does not record any other family relationships beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Talitha's significance in the biblical narrative centers on Jesus' miraculous power over death and illness. At twelve years old, she was raised from death by Jesus, demonstrating His authority and compassion. This event underscores the faith of her father, Jairus, and exemplifies Jesus' role as the giver of life.
